speaker: NAR
text: At Masdar City, two ordinary specimens are about to reveal an extraordinary story.

speaker: HAM
text: A metal sample. A salt crystal. ORBIT explored both inside our scientific simulation.

speaker: RAS
text: Its observations are here, but part of its return map is missing.

speaker: ORB
text: My return route is incomplete.

speaker: ALY
text: It left clues in both worlds. We can work out where it went.

speaker: HAM
text: ORBIT is a virtual explorer. Nobody has shrunk, and nothing has happened to the real samples.

speaker: HAM
text: Your mission is to reconstruct the bonding models, compare the evidence, and restore its route.

speaker: NAR
text: An ordinary sample. An extraordinary hidden world.

speaker: HAM
text: Choose which world to investigate first. You will need evidence from both.

speaker: ALY
text: Inspect before you decide. The first clue might not be the whole answer.

speaker: ORB
text: I recorded positive centres everywhere. Where was the negative charge?

speaker: HAM
text: Use the atomic lens. Inspect the positive metal ion cores and the outer electrons in this simplified model.

speaker: ALY
text: The picture helps us explore, but the interactive model is where we test our explanation.

speaker: HAM
text: Reconstruct the metallic structure. What happens to the valence electrons when the metal forms?

speaker: HAM
text: Now identify the two charged components whose attraction holds this structure together.

speaker: HAM
text: In this model, valence electrons are delocalized throughout the metal. Their attraction to positive metal ion cores is metallic bonding.

speaker: HAM
text: The electrons are still part of the material. Its positive and negative charges balance overall.

speaker: HAM
text: Your evidence restored part of ORBIT's route.

speaker: HAM
text: You created alternating positive and negative metal ions. Does that match the metallic model?

speaker: HAM
text: The electrons have not left the specimen. How could its total charge remain neutral if they disappeared?

speaker: HAM
text: Check whether the electrons belong to fixed pairs, or are delocalized through the whole structure.

speaker: ALY
text: Our model needs to show what attracts what. Two positive cores do not explain the bonding by themselves.

speaker: HAM
text: Save your explanation. Both formation models belong in the evidence record.

speaker: RAS
text: The map is becoming clearer. Keep the evidence, not just the picture.

speaker: NAR
text: Another material. A different arrangement to explain.

speaker: ORB
text: This recorded world contains positive and negative ions. The earlier description does not fit.

speaker: HAM
text: Rewind the simplified formation model. Start with a sodium atom and a chlorine atom.

speaker: HAM
text: Observe what changes when one electron moves from sodium to chlorine.

speaker: HAM
text: Check the particles and their charges. Have the nuclei changed, or only the numbers of electrons?

speaker: HAM
text: Sodium loses one electron and becomes a positive sodium ion. Chlorine gains it and becomes a negative chloride ion.

speaker: HAM
text: Electron transfer forms the ions in this example. Ionic bonding is the electrostatic attraction between the oppositely charged ions.

speaker: HAM
text: Expand the view. Solid sodium chloride is an extended ionic lattice, not a collection of separate sodium chloride molecules.

speaker: ALY
text: We have two formation explanations. Now we can compare the structures they produce.

speaker: HAM
text: Move an electron, not a proton. Changing the proton number would change the element.

speaker: HAM
text: Losing a negative electron makes the sodium ion positive. Check your charge calculation.

speaker: HAM
text: An electron sea describes the metallic model. Which charged particles attract in this ionic structure?

speaker: HAM
text: One pair is not the complete solid. Show how the positive and negative ions repeat through the structure.

speaker: NAR
text: The final recording arrives without a location label.

speaker: ORB
text: I am beside positive metal ion cores, with electrons delocalized throughout the surrounding structure.

speaker: HAM
text: The colours and names are hidden. Which model matches the recording? Support your decision with two observations.

speaker: ALY
text: Then match each formation sequence to its resulting structure. That will complete the route.

speaker: HAM
text: The ionic lattice contains cations and anions. Compare that with the components in ORBIT's description.

speaker: HAM
text: Both bonding types involve electrostatic attraction, but they do not involve the same charged components.

speaker: ALY
text: The colour is only an illustration choice. Use the particles and their attraction as evidence.

speaker: HAM
text: Your location choice needs an explanation. Identify the charged components and what attracts them.

speaker: HAM
text: Your evidence matches the metallic model. The complete comparison restores ORBIT's return map.

speaker: ORB
text: You found me. Route confirmed.

speaker: ALY
text: We found the explorer by understanding the world it described.

speaker: HAM
text: Exactly. The models did not change the real substances. They changed what we could explain.

speaker: HAM
text: You found the route by understanding the bonds.

speaker: RAS
text: The two specimens still look ordinary. Their structures do not.

speaker: NAR
text: Two hidden worlds. Two explanations. One journey completed through evidence.

speaker: HAM
text: Before you finish, explain one difference in how the bonds form and one difference in what holds the structures together.

speaker: NAR
text: Five questions check your understanding. Answer all five, then submit. Four correct answers earns the mission achievement.

speaker: HAM
text: In the metallic model, what happens to the valence electrons?

speaker: HAM
text: Which attraction holds a metallic structure together?

speaker: HAM
text: A sodium atom transfers one electron to a chlorine atom. Which result is correct?

speaker: HAM
text: Which statement correctly separates electron transfer from ionic bonding?

speaker: HAM
text: Model X has positive metal ion cores and delocalized electrons. Model Y has a repeating arrangement of cations and anions. Which comparison is correct?

speaker: HAM
text: Well done. You can explain metallic bonding and distinguish it from ionic bonding.

speaker: HAM
text: Revisit the model linked to your feedback. Then try again using the evidence.
